chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the words of God, Mighty and Majestic:
'They shall have what they were miserly with collared around their necks on the Day of Resurrection.'

So he said: 'O Muhammad! There is no one who withholds anything from the Zakat of his wealth except that God, Mighty and Majestic, will make that, on the Day of Resurrection, a serpent of fire encircling his neck, gnawing at his flesh until he is freed from the Reckoning.'

Then he said: 'It is the word of God, Mighty and Majestic: They shall have what they were miserly with collared around their necks on the Day of Resurrection — meaning what they were miserly with of the Zakat.'

key_terms.الْحِسَاب: The Reckoning — the Day of Judgment accounting; the punishment endures until this process is complete
key_terms.بَخِلُوا: They were miserly/stingy — withholding what is owed; in this context, specifically withholding Zakat
key_terms.ثُعْبَاناً مِنْ نَارٍ: A serpent of fire — the eschatological form taken by the withheld wealth as divine punishment
key_terms.سَيُطَوَّقُونَ: They shall be collared — from the root طوق (to encircle/collar), referring to a torment where withheld wealth is worn as a punishing collar

ai.seo_question: What does Quran 3:180 mean about those who withhold Zakat on the Day of Resurrection?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides an authoritative tafsir of Quran 3:180, explaining that the verse refers specifically to withholding Zakat. The metaphor of the serpent of fire serves as an eschatological punishment: the very wealth withheld is transformed into a fiery serpent that torments the miser throughout the Day of Reckoning. This hadith underscores that Zakat is not merely a financial obligation but a spiritual covenant, and its violation carries severe consequences in the afterlife.
